name: Music Library with Album-Tinted Player
note: The playing album re-tints the whole app: --apv-music-tint is a registered <color> that transitions, every surface derives from it with color-mix(in oklch), and the cover breathes at the album's own BPM while a rotating @property sheen plays across it. Queue rows drag with pointer capture and FLIP (or Alt+Arrow), the songs table is a subgrid that re-sorts with FLIP, and every removal is undoable with Cmd/Ctrl+Z. Set --apv-music-h to 100dvh in an app.

name: Streaming Browse with Spatial Focus
note: Arrow keys move focus spatially by measuring card geometry, then scroll only the component's own row and page scrollers (scrollTo, never scrollIntoView) so the host page stays put; one procedural canvas renderer paints the card art, episode thumbnails, the cross-fading hero backdrop and the player "video". Watching updates Continue Watching with FLIP, My List edits are undoable, and the player has J/K/L, skip intro and captions. Set --apv-stream-h to 100dvh in an app.

name: Podcast Player with Live Transcript
note: The transcript drives the player: each paragraph's words are timed by their share of its characters, one marker glides word to word by measuring the current span, and the reader takes over auto-follow the moment they scroll (Jump to now hands it back). The waveform canvas is derived from the transcript so every dip is a speaker change; chapters, speed-aware end times, a sleep timer, undoable clips and an Up Next menu complete it. Set --apv-pod-h to 100dvh in an app.

name: Photo Library with EXIF Inspector
note: A justified grid computed per section from each photo's aspect ratio: because tiles never change shape, every relayout (zoom slider, Ctrl+wheel pinch, resize, delete) is a FLIP of translate plus uniform scale, and the lightbox opens and closes as a FLIP from the tile. Photos are painted procedurally and develop in as they load, EXIF agrees with each scene, and the info panel's histogram is measured from the painted pixels; Shift-click ranges, Cmd/Ctrl+A, favourites, albums and undoable deletes work throughout. Set --apv-photos-h to 100dvh in an app.

name: Video Editor Timeline
note: A working NLE: clips move between compatible tracks, trim against their source handles, snap to the playhead, markers and every edit point, and land with the overwrite rule real editors use (whatever they cover is trimmed, split or removed), all quantised to 24 fps frames and undoable with Cmd/Ctrl+Z. Filmstrips and waveforms are drawn on one canvas sized to the visible slice of the timeline (cached frames from the same procedural footage the program monitor plays), with J/K/L shuttle, I/O, markers, blade, ripple delete and drag-in from the bin. Set --apv-edit-h to 100dvh in an app.

name: Audiobook Player with Chapter Dial
note: One turn of the dial is one chapter: a registered --apv-book-p number drives a conic-gradient ring and the arm's rotate, dragging past twelve o'clock carries you into the next chapter (or back into the previous one), and an outer SVG ring maps the whole book with chapter arcs and bookmark pips. Speed-aware time left, a wall-clock sleep timer that fades the voice ring, inline-editable bookmarks and an undoable jump history ("was Ch 7 · 12:31") work from the keyboard too. Set --apv-book-h to 100dvh in an app.

name: Stargazing Live Stream with Chat
note: The sky is a DPR-aware canvas (stars rotating about an off-frame pole, a pre-rendered Milky Way band, silhouettes as Path2D) and every meteor is a pure function of the stream second, so the 30-minute rewind bar replays the same sky while chat, which runs on live time, reacts to bright meteors before a viewer who is behind sees them. Slow-mode cooldown is a registered @property conic sweep, @mentions autocomplete as an ARIA combobox, the poll uses largest-remainder rounding so it always totals 100%, and red-light mode is one animated filter over the whole app. Set --apv-live-h to 100dvh in an app.

name: Two-Deck DJ Console with Sync
note: One clock drives everything: decks advance at bpm × (1 + pitch), the scrolling waveforms map pixels to real seconds so synced decks show identical beat spacing, Sync matches tempo and snaps the beat phase (shortest way round), and quantised hot-cue jumps keep the phase so a playing deck never drops a beat. Waveforms are generated from each track's form in bars and drawn in batched canvas paths at the device pixel ratio; faders and EQ knobs share one pointer and keyboard slider model, the library is a subgrid table that re-sorts with FLIP and flags Camelot-compatible tracks within pitch range, and loads are undoable. Set --apv-dj-h to 100dvh in an app.
